slides: Greece wedding cost, explained. Why a single headline figure tells you very little about your own wedding.
Your total is set by decisions only you can make. Island, venue type, month and day, guest numbers, and how much of your guests' travel and accommodation you cover.
Write your wedding down first. Island, date, guest list, events and what you will pay for on your guests' behalf. Send that same brief to every venue, so the quotes describe the same wedding.
Read the package contents, not the name. Ceremony setup, venue hire, catering and drinks, coordination on the day, styling and rooms. Is each item included, an add-on or not offered?
Ask about the items quoted separately. Photography and film, music, hair and makeup, transfers, extra events, official fees, taxes and service charges, and overtime.
Paying from Australia? Ask which currency the quote, deposit and balance are invoiced in, when each payment falls due, and what happens to money paid if plans change.
A civil wedding has its own paperwork, with fees at several steps. Check the documents, notice period and ceremony days with the municipality where you will marry.
Planning a wedding in Greece? Message us to talk it through with a Wedded Advisor. Full guide at the link in bio.
instagram_carousel.caption:
A couple marries at a town hall with a long lunch for close family. Another takes a clifftop venue for the weekend, hosts a welcome dinner and covers ferries for every guest. Same island, same month, and neither total helps the other.

That is why our new guide to the cost of a wedding in Greece gives no headline figure. It explains what shapes your total, what a venue package bundles, what sits outside it, and how paying in euro from Australia works.

Before you ask for quotes:
- Write down your wedding: island, date, guest list, events and what you will cover for guests.
- Send that same brief to every venue and planner.
- Ask whether exclusive use, where your party has the site to itself, is offered for your date.
- Ask which items are charged per guest, and when the final number is locked.
- Ask for every contract in English, with a copy you keep.

Where you stand in Australia:
- Under the consumer guarantees, services must be carried out with an acceptable level of care and skill, and these basic rights can't be taken away by anything a business says or does.
- An overseas business selling directly to Australian consumers must follow the Australian Consumer Law, but a remedy can be hard to obtain in practice, so read the cancellation terms before you pay.
This is general information, not legal advice.

Smartraveller's advice for Greece is to buy comprehensive travel insurance before you leave and read the Product Disclosure Statement closely.
